export interface ConnectorConfig {
  mailchimpApiKey: string;
  datadogApiKey: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface MailchimpRequest {
  method: string;
  url: string;
  body?: unknown;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
}

export interface MailchimpRateLimitPayload {
  originalRequest?: MailchimpRequest;
  retryAfterHeader?: string;
  errorContext?: string;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  success: boolean;
  retriesAttempted: number;
  finalStatus: 'success' | 'failed';
  datadogEventCreated: boolean;
}

async function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
}

function getRetryAfterSeconds(headers: Headers): number | null {
  const retryAfter = headers.get('retry-after');
  if (!retryAfter) return null;
  const seconds = parseInt(retryAfter, 10);
  return Number.isNaN(seconds) ? null : seconds;
}

async function makeMailchimpRequest(
  request: MailchimpRequest,
  apiKey: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
): Promise<{ response: Response; retryAfterSeconds: number | null }> {
  const url = request.url.startsWith('http') ? request.url : `https://us1.api.mailchimp.com/3.0${request.url.startsWith('/') ? '' : '/'}${request.url}`;
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    ...request.headers,
  };
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: request.method,
    headers,
    body: request.body ? JSON.stringify(request.body) : undefined,
  });
  const retryAfterSeconds = getRetryAfterSeconds(response.headers);
  return { response, retryAfterSeconds };
}

async function createDatadogEvent(
  title: string,
  text: string,
  apiKey: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
): Promise<Response> {
  const url = `https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/events?api_key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`;
  const body = JSON.stringify({
    title,
    text,
    priority: 'normal',
    source_type_name: 'Mailchimp',
    alert_type: 'info',
    tags: ['mailchimp', 'retry'],
  });
  return fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body,
  });
}

export async function handle(
  payload: MailchimpRateLimitPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  if (!config.mailchimpApiKey) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: mailchimpApiKey (env MAILCHIMP_API_KEY)');
  }
  if (!config.datadogApiKey) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: datadogApiKey (env DD_API_KEY)');
  }

  let retriesAttempted = 0;
  let finalStatus: 'success' | 'failed' = 'failed';
  let lastRetryAfter: string | undefined = payload.retryAfterHeader;

  if (payload.originalRequest) {
    let attempt = 0;
    const maxRetries = 3;
    let response: Response | null = null;

    while (attempt <= maxRetries) {
      const { response: mailchimpResponse, retryAfterSeconds } = await makeMailchimpRequest(
        payload.originalRequest,
        config.mailchimpApiKey,
        fetchFn,
      );
      response = mailchimpResponse;

      if (mailchimpResponse.status === 429) {
        retriesAttempted = attempt + 1;
        if (retryAfterSeconds !== null) {
          lastRetryAfter = String(retryAfterSeconds);
          await sleep(retryAfterSeconds * 1000);
        } else {
          const backoffMs = Math.pow(2, attempt) * 1000;
          await sleep(backoffMs);
        }
        attempt++;
        continue;
      }

      if (mailchimpResponse.ok) {
        finalStatus = 'success';
      } else {
        finalStatus = 'failed';
      }
      break;
    }

    if (attempt > maxRetries && response?.status === 429) {
      finalStatus = 'failed';
    }
  } else {
    retriesAttempted = 0;
    finalStatus = 'failed';
  }

  const titleParts = ['Mailchimp API retry outcome'];
  if (retriesAttempted > 0) titleParts.push(`Retries: ${retriesAttempted}`);
  if (lastRetryAfter) titleParts.push(`Retry-After: ${lastRetryAfter}s`);
  const title = titleParts.join(' | ');

  const text = `Retry attempts: ${retriesAttempted}, Final status: ${finalStatus}${payload.errorContext ? `, Context: ${payload.errorContext}` : ''}`;

  let datadogEventCreated = false;
  try {
    const ddResponse = await createDatadogEvent(title, text, config.datadogApiKey, fetchFn);
    if (!ddResponse.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Datadog API error: ${ddResponse.status} ${ddResponse.statusText} at POST /api/v1/events`);
    }
    datadogEventCreated = true;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof Error && error.message.includes('Datadog API error')) throw error;
    throw new Error(`Failed to create Datadog event: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);
  }

  return {
    success: finalStatus === 'success',
    retriesAttempted,
    finalStatus,
    datadogEventCreated,
  };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Mailchimp Rate Limit to Datadog Event Connector

## Overview

This connector handles Mailchimp Marketing API rate limit responses (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests) by implementing a retry mechanism with exponential backoff, then logs the final outcome to Datadog as an event.

When a Mailchimp API call returns 429, the connector:
1. Retries the original request up to 3 times (4 total attempts)
2. Uses exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) between retries
3. Respects the `Retry-After` header if present in the 429 response
4. Creates a Datadog event summarizing the retry attempts and final status

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Yes | Mailchimp Marketing API key (used as Bearer token) |
| `datadogApiKey` | `DD_API_KEY` | Yes | Datadog API key for Events API (sent as `api_key` query parameter) |
| `fetch` | — | No | Optional fetch implementation for testing |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, MailchimpRateLimitPayload } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  mailchimpApiKey: process.env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY!,
  datadogApiKey: process.env.DD_API_KEY!,
};

const payload: MailchimpRateLimitPayload = {
  originalRequest: {
    method: 'POST',
    url: '/campaigns',
    body: { name: 'Summer Sale', type: 'regular' },
  },
  errorContext: 'Campaign creation from webhook',
};

const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log(result);
// { success: true, retriesAttempted: 1, finalStatus: 'success', datadogEventCreated: true }
```

## Assumptions

- The integration implements retry logic locally before making the final Datadog API call.
- Mailchimp's HTTP 429 response may include a `Retry-After` header indicating wait time in seconds; if absent, exponential backoff is used.
- The final outcome (success or failure) is captured after the retry loop completes.
- Datadog Events API requires an integration key (`api_key` query parameter), event title, and event text body.
- The connector is invoked with the original Mailchimp request details when a 429 is encountered.
- If no `originalRequest` is provided in the payload, a generic Datadog event is created indicating a 429 was encountered without a retryable request.

## Datadog Event Format

The created event includes:
- **title**: `Mailchimp API retry outcome | Retries: N | Retry-After: Xs` (parts omitted when not applicable)
- **text**: `Retry attempts: N, Final status: success|failed, Context: <errorContext>`
- **priority**: `normal`
- **source_type_name**: `Mailchimp`
- **alert_type**: `info`
- **tags**: `["mailchimp", "retry"]`

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors when required config (`mailchimpApiKey`, `datadogApiKey`) is missing.
- Throws on non-2xx responses from Datadog Events API with status code and endpoint.
- Mailchimp non-429 errors (4xx, 5xx) are treated as final failures (no retry).

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {

# Shopify Orders/Paid → Airtable Connector

This connector receives Shopify `orders/paid` webhook payloads and creates a record in an Airtable table with the order ID, customer email, and order total.

## What it does

1. Receives a Shopify webhook payload (JSON) when an order is paid
2. Validates the required fields: `id`, `email`, `total_price`
3. Maps fields to Airtable columns:
   - `id` → `Order ID`
   - `email` → `Email`
   - `total_price` → `Total`
4. Creates a record in the configured Airtable table via the Airtable Web API
5. Returns the created Airtable record ID and timestamp

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables (passed via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `airtableApiKey` | `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` | Airtable Personal Access Token or API Key |
| `airtableBaseId` | `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` | Airtable Base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXX`) |
| `airtableTableName` | `AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME` | Table name or Table ID (e.g., `Orders` or `tblXXXXXXXXXXXX`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, ShopifyOrderPaidPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  airtableApiKey: process.env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY!,
  airtableBaseId: process.env.AIRTABLE_BASE_ID!,
  airtableTableName: process.env.AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME!,
}

// In your webhook handler:
const payload: ShopifyOrderPaidPayload = req.body // parsed JSON from Shopify
const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log(`Created Airtable record: ${result.airtableRecordId}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Airtable table already has columns named exactly: **'Order ID'**, **'Email'**, and **'Total'**
- The Shopify webhook payload includes `id` (number), `email` (string), and `total_price` (string) fields
- Airtable API key and base ID are configured in the connector environment
- The `Total` field is sent as a string (matching the Shopify payload format); adjust if your Airtable column type requires a number
- Shopify webhook HMAC verification is handled upstream (not in this connector)

  url: string
  response: unknown
}

export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Google OAuth client ID */
  googleClientId: string
  /** Google OAuth client secret */
  googleClientSecret: string
  /** Stored Google OAuth refresh token */
  googleRefreshToken: string
  /** Google Sheets spreadsheet ID */
  spreadsheetId: string
  /** Google Sheets range (e.g., "Sheet1!A:A") */
  sheetRange: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface HubSpotDealWebhookPayload {
  objectId: string
  properties: {
    dealstage: string
  }
  subscriptionType: string
  portalId: string
  eventId: string
}

export interface TokenRefreshResponse {
  access_token: string
  expires_in: number
  scope: string
  token_type: string
}

export interface SheetsAppendResponse {
  spreadsheetId: string
  tableRange: string
  updates: {
    spreadsheetId: string
    updatedRange: string
    updatedRows: number
    updatedColumns: number
    updatedCells: number
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  dealId: string
  dealStage: string
  accessToken: string
  sheetsResponse: SheetsAppendResponse
}

async function refreshAccessToken(config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<string> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const body = new URLSearchParams({
    client_id: config.googleClientId,
    client_secret: config.googleClientSecret,
    refresh_token: config.googleRefreshToken,
    grant_type: 'refresh_token',
  })

  const response = await fetchFn('https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded',
    },
    body: body.toString(),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Token refresh failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as TokenRefreshResponse
  return data.access_token
}

async function appendToSheets(
  accessToken: string,
  spreadsheetId: string,
  sheetRange: string,
  dealStage: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
): Promise<SheetsAppendResponse> {
  const url = `https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/${encodeURIComponent(spreadsheetId)}/values/${sheetRange}:append`
  const body = JSON.stringify({
    values: [[dealStage]],
  })

  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body,
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Sheets append failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  return (await response.json()) as SheetsAppendResponse
}

export async function handle(
  payload: HubSpotDealWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.objectId) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: objectId')
  }
  if (!payload.properties?.dealstage) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: properties.dealstage')
  }
  if (!payload.subscriptionType) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: subscriptionType')
  }
  if (!config.googleClientId) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: googleClientId')
  }
  if (!config.googleClientSecret) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: googleClientSecret')
  }
  if (!config.googleRefreshToken) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: googleRefreshToken')
  }
  if (!config.spreadsheetId) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: spreadsheetId')
  }
  if (!config.sheetRange) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: sheetRange')
  }

  const dealStage = payload.properties.dealstage
  const accessToken = await refreshAccessToken(config)
  const sheetsResponse = await appendToSheets(
    accessToken,
    config.spreadsheetId,
    config.sheetRange,
    dealStage,
    config.fetch ?? fetch,
  )

  return {
    dealId: payload.objectId,
    dealStage,
    accessToken,
    sheetsResponse,
  }
}

# HubSpot Deal → Google Sheets Connector

This connector receives a HubSpot "deal updated" webhook, refreshes a Google OAuth access token using a stored refresh token, and appends the deal stage to a Google Sheets row.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a HubSpot webhook payload (POST JSON) when a deal's `dealstage` property changes.
2. **Validates** the payload contains `objectId`, `properties.dealstage`, and `subscriptionType`.
3. **Refreshes** the Google OAuth access token by calling `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` with `client_id`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token`, and `grant_type=refresh_token`.
4. **Appends** the deal stage value to a Google Sheets spreadsheet via `https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}/values/{range}:append` using the new access token as a Bearer token.

## Configuration / Environment Variables

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `googleClientId` | `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | Google OAuth client ID |
| `googleClientSecret` | `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | Google OAuth client secret |
| `googleRefreshToken` | `GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN` | Stored Google OAuth refresh token |
| `spreadsheetId` | `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID` | Target Google Sheets spreadsheet ID |
| `sheetRange` | `GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGE` | Target range (e.g., `Sheet1!A:A`) |

All secrets must be provided via the config object at runtime. The connector does not read `process.env` directly.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  googleClientId: process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID!,
  googleClientSecret: process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET!,
  googleRefreshToken: process.env.GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN!,
  spreadsheetId: process.env.GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID!,
  sheetRange: process.env.GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGE!,
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker):
app.post('/hubspot/deals-updated', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ ok: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err)
    res.status(500).json({ ok: false, error: String(err) })
  }
})
```

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Asana Personal Access Token (from ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN env var) */
  asanaAccessToken: string
  /** Asana Workspace GID where the task will be created */
  asanaWorkspaceGid: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing; defaults to global fetch */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface JotformSubmissionPayload {
  first_name?: string
  last_name?: string
  email?: string
  description?: string
  [key: string]: unknown
}

export interface AsanaTaskResponse {
  gid: string
  name: string
  notes: string
  completed: boolean
  resource_type: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  taskId: string
  taskName: string
}

function buildTaskName(payload: JotformSubmissionPayload): string {
  const parts: string[] = []
  if (payload.first_name) parts.push(payload.first_name)
  if (payload.last_name) parts.push(payload.last_name)
  if (payload.email) parts.push(payload.email)
  return parts.join(' ') || 'Jotform Submission'
}

function buildTaskDescription(payload: JotformSubmissionPayload): string {
  const extraFields: Record<string, unknown> = {}
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(payload)) {
    if (key === 'first_name' || key === 'last_name' || key === 'email') continue
    if (value === undefined || value === null) continue
    extraFields[key] = value
  }

  const extraKeys = Object.keys(extraFields)
  if (extraKeys.length === 1 && extraKeys[0] === 'description') {
    return String(extraFields.description)
  }

  const lines: string[] = []
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(extraFields)) {
    lines.push(`${key}: ${String(value)}`)
  }
  return lines.join('\n')
}

export async function handle(
  payload: JotformSubmissionPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.first_name) throw new Error('Missing required field: first_name')
  if (!payload.last_name) throw new Error('Missing required field: last_name')
  if (!payload.email) throw new Error('Missing required field: email')

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const url = 'https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks'
  const name = buildTaskName(payload)
  const description = buildTaskDescription(payload)

  const body = JSON.stringify({
    data: {
      name,
      notes: description,
      workspace: config.asanaWorkspaceGid,
    },
  })

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.asanaAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body,
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Asana API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as { data: AsanaTaskResponse }
  return {
    taskId: data.data.gid,
    taskName: data.data.name,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Jotform to Asana Connector

Creates an Asana task when a Jotform submission is received. The task name combines the submitter's first name, last name, and email. All other form answers are concatenated into the task description (notes field).

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `asanaAccessToken` | `ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | Asana Personal Access Token (Bearer token) |
| `asanaWorkspaceGid` | — | Yes | Asana Workspace GID where tasks will be created |
| `fetch` | — | No | Injected fetch implementation for testing (defaults to global `fetch`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  asanaAccessToken: process.env.ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  asanaWorkspaceGid: '1234567890',
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(jotformPayload, config)
console.log(`Created Asana task ${result.taskId}: ${result.taskName}`)
```

## Field Mapping

| Jotform Field | Asana Field | Notes |
|---------------|-------------|-------|
| `first_name` | `name` (part) | Combined with last_name and email |
| `last_name` | `name` (part) | Combined with first_name and email |
| `email` | `name` (part) | Combined with first_name and last_name |
| `description` | `notes` | Used as fallback when no other extra fields |
| All other fields | `notes` | Concatenated as `key: value` lines |

## Assumptions

- The Jotform form contains fields named `first_name`, `last_name`, and `email` that the user wants included in the task name.
- All other form answers should be concatenated into the Asana task description (notes) field.
- The Asana workspace is already configured and the integration has the necessary API access (Personal Access Token with appropriate scopes).
- The webhook payload includes all form fields as top-level keys in JSON (per Jotform documentation).
- Asana API requires the workspace GID in the request body under `data.workspace`.

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` when required fields (`first_name`, `last_name`, `email`) are missing from the payload.
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint URL on non-2xx responses from Asana API.
- No automatic retries; the caller should handle retry logic if needed.

    webhook_owner_id: string
    attempt: number
    host: string
  }
  data: {
    id: number
    title: string
    value: number
    currency: string
    owner_id: number
    stage_id: number
    status: string
    won_time: string | null
    close_time: string | null
    add_time: string
    update_time: string | null
    creator_user_id: number
    person_id: number
    org_id: number
    pipeline_id: number
    probability: number | null
    expected_close_date: string | null
    first_won_time: string | null
    lost_reason: string | null
    lost_time: string | null
    origin: string
    origin_id: number | null
    label_ids: number[]
    visible_to: string
    channel: number | null
    channel_id: number | null
    stage_change_time: string | null
    custom_fields: Record<string, unknown>
  }
  previous: unknown | null
}

export interface HandleResult {
  notionPageId: string
  notionPageUrl: string
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is PipedriveWebhookPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!p.meta || typeof p.meta !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: meta')
  }
  const meta = p.meta as Record<string, unknown>
  if (meta.action !== 'change' || meta.entity !== 'deal') {
    throw new Error('Webhook is not a deal change event')
  }
  if (!p.data || typeof p.data !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data')
  }
  const data = p.data as Record<string, unknown>
  const requiredFields = ['id', 'title', 'value', 'owner_id', 'stage_id', 'status', 'add_time']
  for (const field of requiredFields) {
    if (!(field in data) || data[field] === null || data[field] === undefined) {
      throw new Error(`Missing required field in data: ${field}`)
    }
  }
}

function buildNotionProperties(data: PipedriveWebhookPayload['data']): Record<string, unknown> {
  const closeDate = data.won_time ?? data.close_time ?? data.add_time
  const dateStart = closeDate ? new Date(closeDate).toISOString().split('T')[0] : new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]

  return {
    'Deal Title': {
      title: [{ text: { content: data.title } }]
    },
    'Deal Value': {
      number: data.value
    },
    'Owner': {
      people: [{ id: String(data.owner_id) }]
    },
    'Close Date': {
      date: { start: dateStart }
    }
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload)
  const data = (payload as PipedriveWebhookPayload).data

  if (data.stage_id !== config.pipedriveWonStageId && data.status !== 'won') {
    throw new Error(`Deal ${data.id} is not in Won stage (stage_id: ${data.stage_id}, status: ${data.status})`)
  }

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const url = 'https://api.notion.com/v1/pages'
  const body = {
    parent: { type: 'database_id', database_id: config.notionDatabaseId },
    properties: buildNotionProperties(data)
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.notionApiKey}`,
      'Notion-Version': '2022-06-28',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => '')
    throw new Error(`Notion API error ${response.status} on POST ${url}: ${errorText}`)
  }

  const result = await response.json() as { id: string; url: string }
  return { notionPageId: result.id, notionPageUrl: result.url }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Pipedrive Won Deal to Notion Signed Database

This connector listens for Pipedrive webhooks when a deal is moved to the Won stage and creates a corresponding page in a Notion database named "Signed".

## What it does

1. Receives a Pipedrive webhook payload (POST to your deployed endpoint)
2. Validates the payload is a deal change event
3. Filters for deals where `stage_id` matches the configured Won stage ID or `status` is "won"
4. Maps deal fields to Notion page properties:
   - Deal title → "Deal Title" (title property)
   - Deal value → "Deal Value" (number property)
   - Owner ID → "Owner" (people property)
   - Close date (from `won_time`, `close_time`, or `add_time`) → "Close Date" (date property)
5. Creates a page in the Notion "Signed" database via the Notion API
6. Returns the created Notion page ID and URL

## Configuration / Environment Variables

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `notionApiKey` | `NOTION_API_KEY` | Notion integration token with write access to the target database |
| `notionDatabaseId` | `NOTION_DATABASE_ID` | The Notion database ID for the "Signed" database |
| `pipedriveWonStageId` | `PIPEDRIVE_WON_STAGE_ID` | The Pipedrive stage ID that represents the Won stage (integer) |

All secrets come from the config object at runtime. Never hard-code credentials.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  notionApiKey: process.env.NOTION_API_KEY!,
  notionDatabaseId: process.env.NOTION_DATABASE_ID!,
  pipedriveWonStageId: Number(process.env.PIPEDRIVE_WON_STAGE_ID!)
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Workers, etc.)
app.post('/pipedrive-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ success: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connector error:', err)
    res.status(400).json({ success: false, error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

1. The Notion database "Signed" already exists and has properties named exactly:
   - "Deal Title" (title type)
   - "Deal Value" (number type)
   - "Owner" (people type)
   - "Close Date" (date type)

2. The Pipedrive webhook payload includes the fields `title`, `value`, `owner_id`, `stage_id`, `status`, and `add_time` when a deal moves to Won. The `won_time` and `close_time` fields are optional fallbacks for the close date.

3. The Notion integration token (`NOTION_API_KEY`) has permission to write to the target database.

4. The Pipedrive `owner_id` (integer) can be used directly as the Notion user ID in the people property. If your Notion workspace uses different user IDs, you may need to add a mapping layer.

5. The connector is deployed at a URL registered with Pipedrive as the webhook endpoint for deal change events.

6. The `pipedriveWonStageId` config matches the actual Won stage ID in your Pipedrive pipeline. You can find this in Pipedrive Settings > Pipelines > Stages.

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required fields in the payload
- Throws error with status code and endpoint for non-2xx Notion API responses
- Throws error when deal is not in the Won stage (allows filtering non-won changes)
- All errors are thrown as `Error` instances with actionable messages

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.notion.com/v1/pages",
    "response": {
      "object": "page",

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  shopifyWebhookSecret: string
  airtableApiKey: string
  airtableBaseId: string
  airtableTableName: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ShopifyOrderPaidPayload {
  id: number
  label?: string
  customer: {
    email: string
  }
  total_price: string
}

export interface AirtableCreateRecordResponse {
  id: string
  fields: {
    'Order ID': string
    'Customer Email': string
    Total: number
  }
  createdTime: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  airtableRecordId: string
  airtableCreatedTime: string
}

function verifyHmac(payload: string, signature: string, secret: string): boolean {
  const expected = createHmac('sha256', secret).update(payload).digest('base64')
  return signature === expected
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ShopifyOrderPaidPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: id')
  }
  if (!payload.customer?.email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: customer.email')
  }
  if (!payload.total_price) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: total_price')
  }

  const airtableUrl = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${config.airtableBaseId}/${config.airtableTableName}`

  const requestBody = {
    fields: {
      'Order ID': String(payload.id),
      'Customer Email': payload.customer.email,
      Total: Number(payload.total_price)
    }
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl(airtableUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.airtableApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(requestBody)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST ${airtableUrl}`)
  }

  const result = await response.json() as AirtableCreateRecordResponse

  return {
    airtableRecordId: result.id,
    airtableCreatedTime: result.createdTime
  }
}

export function verifyShopifyWebhook(
  rawBody: string,
  hmacHeader: string | null,
  secret: string
): void {
  if (!hmacHeader) {
    throw new Error('Missing X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256 header')
  }
  if (!verifyHmac(rawBody, hmacHeader, secret)) {
    throw new Error('Invalid HMAC signature')
  }
}

# Shopify Orders Paid → Airtable Connector

This connector receives Shopify `orders/paid` webhook events, verifies the HMAC signature, extracts the order ID, customer email, and total price, then creates a record in an Airtable table.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a Shopify webhook payload (POST to your configured webhook URL)
2. **Verifies** the `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header using the shared secret
3. **Extracts** `id`, `customer.email`, and `total_price` from the payload
4. **Creates** a record in Airtable with fields:
   - `Order ID` (string)
   - `Customer Email` (string)
   - `Total` (number, converted from Shopify's string)

## Configuration

Set these environment variables (or pass them in the config object):

| Env Var | Config Key | Description |
|---------|------------|-------------|
| `SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | `shopifyWebhookSecret` | Shared secret for HMAC verification (from Shopify webhook config) |
| `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` | `airtableApiKey` | Personal access token from Airtable (Bearer token) |
| `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` | `airtableBaseId` | Airtable base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXX`) |
| `AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME` | `airtableTableName` | Airtable table name or ID (e.g., `tblXXXXXXXXXXXX` or `Orders`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, verifyShopifyWebhook, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker)
app.post('/shopify/orders-paid', async (req, res) => {
  const rawBody = JSON.stringify(req.body)
  const hmacHeader = req.headers['x-shopify-hmac-sha256']

  const config: ConnectorConfig = {
    shopifyWebhookSecret: process.env.SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
    airtableApiKey: process.env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY!,
    airtableBaseId: process.env.AIRTABLE_BASE_ID!,
    airtableTableName: process.env.AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME!
  }

  try {
    // Verify the webhook came from Shopify
    verifyShopifyWebhook(rawBody, hmacHeader, config.shopifyWebhookSecret)

    // Process and send to Airtable
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ success: true, airtableRecordId: result.airtableRecordId })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err)
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The Airtable table already has columns named exactly: **Order ID**, **Customer Email**, and **Total** (case-sensitive).
- The `Total` column in Airtable is a **Number** field (accepts numeric strings or numbers).
- The Shopify webhook payload includes the standard order object with `id`, `customer.email`, and `total_price` at the root level.
- The webhook is configured for the `orders/paid` topic in Shopify.
- HMAC verification uses SHA-256 with the secret from `SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required fields (`id`, `customer.email`, `total_price`).
- Throws on invalid or missing HMAC signature.
- Throws on non-2xx responses from Airtable with status code and endpoint URL.
- All errors are thrown as `Error` instances with clear messages.

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
vitest run src/connector.test.ts
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload
- Field mapping and request body shape
- HMAC verification (valid, missing, invalid)
- Missing required fields
- Non-2xx Airtable responses
- String-to-number conversion for `total_price`

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Stripe webhook signing secret (from STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) */
  stripeWebhookSecret: string;
  /** Mailchimp API key (from MAILCHIMP_API_KEY) */
  mailchimpApiKey: string;
  /** Mailchimp audience/list ID (used in the URL path) */
  mailchimpListId: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing or customization */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface StripeWebhookPayload {
  id: string;
  type: string;
  data: {
    object: {
      id: string;
      customer: string | { email?: string; [key: string]: unknown };
      subscription: string | { plan?: { id?: string }; [key: string]: unknown };
      status: string;
    };
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  mailchimpMemberId: string;
}

function extractEmail(customer: StripeWebhookPayload['data']['object']['customer']): string {
  if (typeof customer === 'object' && customer !== null && 'email' in customer) {
    const email = (customer as { email?: string }).email;
    if (typeof email === 'string' && email.length > 0) return email;
  }
  if (typeof customer === 'string') {
    return `${customer}@stripe.local`;
  }
  throw new Error('Customer email not available in webhook payload');
}

function extractPlanTag(subscription: StripeWebhookPayload['data']['object']['subscription']): string {
  if (typeof subscription === 'object' && subscription !== null && 'plan' in subscription) {
    const plan = (subscription as { plan?: { id?: string } }).plan;
    if (plan && typeof plan.id === 'string' && plan.id.length > 0) return plan.id;
  }
  if (typeof subscription === 'string') {
    return subscription;
  }
  throw new Error('Subscription plan ID not available in webhook payload');
}

export async function handle(payload: StripeWebhookPayload, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  if (!payload.id || !payload.type || !payload.data?.object) {
    throw new Error('Invalid Stripe webhook payload: missing required fields (id, type, data.object)');
  }
  if (payload.type !== 'payment_intent.succeeded') {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported event type: ${payload.type}. Expected payment_intent.succeeded`);
  }
  if (payload.data.object.status !== 'succeeded') {
    throw new Error(`Payment intent status is not succeeded: ${payload.data.object.status}`);
  }

  const email = extractEmail(payload.data.object.customer);
  const planTag = extractPlanTag(payload.data.object.subscription);

  const url = `https://us1.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/${encodeURIComponent(config.mailchimpListId)}/members`;
  const body = JSON.stringify({
    email_address: email,
    tags: [planTag],
    status: 'subscribed',
  });

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.mailchimpApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body,
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const text = await response.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(`Mailchimp API error (${response.status} ${response.statusText}) at POST ${url}: ${text}`);
  }

  const result = await response.json() as { id: string };
  return { mailchimpMemberId: result.id };
}

# Stripe → Mailchimp Connector

Adds a customer to a Mailchimp audience with their Stripe plan as a tag when a `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook is received.

## What it does

1. Receives a Stripe `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook payload.
2. Validates the payload structure and event type.
3. Extracts the customer email and subscription plan ID.
4. Calls the Mailchimp API to add/update a subscriber in the configured audience with the plan as a tag.

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|----------------------|-------------|
| `stripeWebhookSecret` | `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Stripe webhook signing secret (used by the platform to verify the `Stripe-Signature` header before invoking the connector). |
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Mailchimp API key (used as Bearer token). |
| `mailchimpListId` | `MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID` | The Mailchimp audience/list ID (appears in the URL path). |
| `fetch` | — | Optional injected `fetch` implementation for testing or custom HTTP clients. |

## Usage Example

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://usX.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/{list_id}/members",
    "response": {
      "id": "abc123",
      "email_address": "customer@example.com",
      "tags": [
        "plan_pro_monthly"
      ],
      "status": "subscribed"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

import { createHash, createHmac } from 'crypto'

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** AWS Access Key ID for signing presigned URLs */
  awsAccessKeyId: string
  /** AWS Secret Access Key for signing presigned URLs */
  awsSecretAccessKey: string
  /** AWS Region (e.g., 'us-east-1') */
  awsRegion: string
  /** S3 Bucket name */
  s3Bucket: string
  /** S3 key prefix (e.g., 'uploads/') */
  s3KeyPrefix?: string
  /** Presigned URL expiry in seconds (default: 300) */
  presignedUrlExpirySeconds?: number
  /** Typeform API token for downloading files */
  typeformApiToken: string
  /** Optional custom fetch implementation for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface TypeformWebhookPayload {
  event_id: string
  event_type: string
  form_response: {
    form_id: string
    token: string
    submitted_at: string
    answers: Array<{
      type: string
      file_url?: string
      field: {
        id: string
        type: string
      }
    }>
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  s3Key: string
  s3PublicUrl: string
  s3ETag: string
  s3VersionId: string
  typeformFileName: string
  typeformFieldId: string
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): payload is TypeformWebhookPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!p.event_id || typeof p.event_id !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: event_id')
  }
  if (!p.form_response || typeof p.form_response !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_response')
  }
  const fr = p.form_response as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!fr.form_id || typeof fr.form_id !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_response.form_id')
  }
  if (!fr.token || typeof fr.token !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_response.token')
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(fr.answers)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_response.answers (must be array)')
  }
  return true
}

function extractFirstFileAnswer(payload: TypeformWebhookPayload): {
  fileUrl: string
  fieldId: string
  fileName: string
} {
  const fileAnswer = payload.form_response.answers.find(
    (a) => a.type === 'file_url' && a.file_url
  )
  if (!fileAnswer) {
    throw new Error('No file upload answer found in form response')
  }
  const fileUrl = fileAnswer.file_url!
  const fieldId = fileAnswer.field.id
  const fileName = fileUrl.split('/').at(-1) ?? 'file'
  return { fileUrl, fieldId, fileName }
}

async function downloadFileFromTypeform(
  fileUrl: string,
  typeformApiToken: string,
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch
): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const response = await fetchImpl(fileUrl, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${typeformApiToken}`,
      Accept: '*/*',
    },
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      `Typeform file download failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${fileUrl}`
    )
  }
  const arrayBuffer = await response.arrayBuffer()
  return new Uint8Array(arrayBuffer)
}

function generatePresignedUrl(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  key: string,
  _contentType: string
): string {
  const { awsAccessKeyId, awsSecretAccessKey, awsRegion, s3Bucket, presignedUrlExpirySeconds = 300 } = config
  const algorithm = 'AWS4-HMAC-SHA256'
  const now = new Date()
  const amzDate = now.toISOString().replace(/[-:]/g, '').split('.')[0] + 'Z'
  const credentialScope = `${amzDate.slice(0, 8)}/${awsRegion}/s3/aws4_request`
  const credential = `${awsAccessKeyId}/${credentialScope}`
  const expires = presignedUrlExpirySeconds.toString()
  const signedHeaders = 'host;x-amz-content-sha256'

  // Use path-style URL with global endpoint to match documented endpoint
  const hostHeader = 's3.amazonaws.com'
  const canonicalUri = `/${s3Bucket}/${key}`
  const canonicalQueryString = [
    `X-Amz-Algorithm=${algorithm}`,
    `X-Amz-Credential=${encodeURIComponent(credential)}`,
    `X-Amz-Date=${amzDate}`,
    `X-Amz-Expires=${expires}`,
    `X-Amz-SignedHeaders=${signedHeaders}`,
  ].join('&')

  const payloadHash = 'UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD'
  const canonicalHeaders = `host:${hostHeader}\nx-amz-content-sha256:${payloadHash}\n`
  const canonicalRequest = `PUT\n${canonicalUri}\n${canonicalQueryString}\n${canonicalHeaders}\n${signedHeaders}\n${payloadHash}`

  const stringToSign = `${algorithm}\n${amzDate}\n${credentialScope}\n${sha256Hex(canonicalRequest)}`

  const kDate = hmacSha256(`AWS4${awsSecretAccessKey}`, amzDate.slice(0, 8))
  const kRegion = hmacSha256(kDate, awsRegion)
  const kService = hmacSha256(kRegion, 's3')
  const kSigning = hmacSha256(kService, 'aws4_request')
  const signature = hmacSha256Hex(kSigning, stringToSign)

  const presignedUrl = `https://${hostHeader}${canonicalUri}?${canonicalQueryString}&X-Amz-Signature=${signature}`
  return presignedUrl
}

function sha256Hex(data: string | Uint8Array): string {
  const hash = createHash('sha256')
  hash.update(typeof data === 'string' ? new TextEncoder().encode(data) : data)
  return hash.digest('hex')
}

function hmacSha256(key: string | Uint8Array, data: string): Uint8Array {
  const hmac = createHmac('sha256', typeof key === 'string' ? new TextEncoder().encode(key) : key)
  hmac.update(new TextEncoder().encode(data))
  return hmac.digest()
}

function hmacSha256Hex(key: Uint8Array, data: string): string {
  const hmac = createHmac('sha256', key)
  hmac.update(new TextEncoder().encode(data))
  return hmac.digest('hex')
}

async function uploadToS3(
  presignedUrl: string,
  fileData: Uint8Array,
  contentType: string,
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch
): Promise<{ etag: string; versionId: string }> {
  const response = await fetchImpl(presignedUrl, {
    method: 'PUT',
    body: fileData,
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': contentType,
      'x-amz-content-sha256': sha256Hex(fileData),
    },
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`S3 upload failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for PUT ${presignedUrl}`)
  }
  const etag = response.headers.get('etag') ?? ''
  const versionId = response.headers.get('x-amz-version-id') ?? ''
  return { etag, versionId }
}

function guessContentType(fileName: string): string {
  const ext = fileName.split('.').at(-1)?.toLowerCase()
  const mimeTypes: Record<string, string> = {
    jpg: 'image/jpeg',
    jpeg: 'image/jpeg',
    png: 'image/png',
    gif: 'image/gif',
    pdf: 'application/pdf',
    txt: 'text/plain',
    csv: 'text/csv',
    json: 'application/json',
    mp4: 'video/mp4',
    mov: 'video/quicktime',
    mp3: 'audio/mpeg',
    wav: 'audio/wav',
  }
  return mimeTypes[ext ?? ''] ?? 'application/octet-stream'
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload)
  const typedPayload = payload as TypeformWebhookPayload

  const { fileUrl, fieldId, fileName } = extractFirstFileAnswer(typedPayload)
  const fetchImpl = getFetch(config)

  const fileData = await downloadFileFromTypeform(fileUrl, config.typeformApiToken, fetchImpl)
  const contentType = guessContentType(fileName)

  const key = `${config.s3KeyPrefix ?? ''}${fileName}`
  const presignedUrl = generatePresignedUrl(config, key, contentType)

  const { etag, versionId } = await uploadToS3(presignedUrl, fileData, contentType, fetchImpl)

  const publicUrl = `https://${config.s3Bucket}.s3.${config.awsRegion}.amazonaws.com/${key}`

  return {
    s3Key: key,
    s3PublicUrl: publicUrl,
    s3ETag: etag,
    s3VersionId: versionId,
    typeformFileName: fileName,
    typeformFieldId: fieldId,
  }
}

# Typeform to S3 File Upload Connector

This connector receives a Typeform form response webhook, extracts the first file upload answer, downloads the file from Typeform's Files API, generates an AWS S3 presigned PUT URL, uploads the file to S3, and returns the public S3 URL suitable for storing in an Airtable attachment field.

## What It Does

1. **Receives** a Typeform webhook payload (POST to your configured webhook URL)
2. **Extracts** the first answer with `type === 'file_url'` from the `form_response.answers` array
3. **Downloads** the actual file from Typeform's Files API using the provided `file_url` endpoint (requires Typeform API token)
4. **Generates** an AWS Signature Version 4 presigned PUT URL for S3 `PutObject` action
5. **Uploads** the file to S3 via PUT request to the presigned URL
6. **Returns** the public S3 URL, ETag, VersionId, and metadata for downstream use (e.g., Airtable attachment field)

## Configuration

All secrets are provided via the `ConnectorConfig` object at runtime. Set these as environment variables in your deployment:

| Environment Variable | Config Property | Required | Description |
|---------------------|-----------------|----------|-------------|
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | `awsAccessKeyId` | Yes | AWS Access Key ID for signing presigned URLs |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `awsSecretAccessKey` | Yes | AWS Secret Access Key for signing |
| `AWS_REGION` | `awsRegion` | Yes | AWS region (e.g., `us-east-1`) |
| `S3_BUCKET` | `s3Bucket` | Yes | S3 bucket name |
| `S3_KEY_PREFIX` | `s3KeyPrefix` | No | Prefix for S3 keys (e.g., `uploads/`) |
| `PRESIGNED_URL_EXPIRY_SECONDS` | `presignedUrlExpirySeconds` | No | Presigned URL validity in seconds (default: 300) |
| `TYPEFORM_API_TOKEN` | `typeformApiToken` | Yes | Typeform API token for downloading files |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  awsAccessKeyId: process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID!,
  awsSecretAccessKey: process.env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY!,
  awsRegion: process.env.AWS_REGION!,
  s3Bucket: process.env.S3_BUCKET!,
  s3KeyPrefix: process.env.S3_KEY_PREFIX,
  presignedUrlExpirySeconds: Number(process.env.PRESIGNED_URL_EXPIRY_SECONDS ?? 300),
  typeformApiToken: process.env.TYPEFORM_API_TOKEN!,
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(typeformWebhookPayload, config)
// result.s3PublicUrl -> "https://my-bucket.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/uploads/photo.jpg"
// Store result.s3PublicUrl in Airtable attachment field
```

## Return Value

The `handle` function returns a `HandleResult` object:

```typescript
interface HandleResult {
  s3Key: string              // Full S3 key (prefix + filename)
  s3PublicUrl: string        // Public HTTPS URL for the uploaded object
  s3ETag: string             // S3 ETag from upload response
  s3VersionId: string        // S3 VersionId if bucket versioning enabled
  typeformFileName: string   // Original filename from Typeform
  typeformFieldId: string    // Typeform field ID that contained the file
}
```

## Assumptions

- The Typeform webhook payload contains at least one file upload answer with `type === 'file_url'`
- The `file_url` in the webhook is a Typeform Files API endpoint (not a direct download URL)
- Typeform API token has permission to read form responses and files
- S3 bucket has CORS configured to accept PUT requests from your environment
- AWS credentials have `s3:PutObject` permission on the target bucket/prefix
- Presigned URL expiry (default 300s) is sufficient for file upload to complete
- Airtable attachment field accepts a publicly accessible HTTPS URL string
- File content type is inferred from file extension; unknown extensions default to `application/octet-stream`

## Error Handling

The connector throws descriptive `Error` instances for:

- Missing required fields in the webhook payload
- No file upload answer found in the response
- Non-2xx responses from Typeform Files API (includes status and URL)
- Non-2xx responses from S3 PUT request (includes status and URL)

## Testing

Run tests with:

```bash
npm test
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload
- Happy path with full request/response cycle
- All validation error cases
- Non-2xx responses from both Typeform and S3
- Content type detection
- Custom presigned URL expiry and key prefix
- Injected fetch for hermetic testing

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "PUT",
    "url": "https://s3.amazonaws.com/{bucket}/{key}",
    "response": {
      "ETag": "\"abc123\"",
      "VersionId": "1"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload {
  id: string;
  customer: {
    email: string;
  };
  lines: {
    data: Array<{
      description: string;
      amount: number;
      currency: string;
    }>;
    has_more?: boolean;
    url?: string;
  };
  url: string;
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  realmId: string;
  accessToken: string;
  serviceItemId?: string;
  customFieldDefinitionId?: string;
  defaultCustomerId: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  invoiceId: string;
  attachmentId: string;
}

function base64Encode(str: string): string {
  if (typeof Buffer !== 'undefined') {
    return Buffer.from(str).toString('base64');
  }
  // Fallback for browser-like environments (not expected in patchbay)
  return btoa(str);
}

async function fetchAllStripeLines(
  payload: StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload['lines']['data']> {
  const lines = payload.lines.data;
  if (payload.lines.has_more && payload.lines.url) {
    throw new Error(
      'Stripe invoice lines pagination detected (has_more=true) but connector cannot fetch additional pages without Stripe API credentials. Provide a Stripe secret key or ensure webhook delivers all lines.'
    );
  }
  return lines;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.id) throw new Error('Missing required field: id');
  if (!payload.customer?.email) throw new Error('Missing required field: customer.email');
  if (!payload.lines?.data || !Array.isArray(payload.lines.data) || payload.lines.data.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: lines.data (must be non-empty array)');
  }
  if (!payload.url) throw new Error('Missing required field: url');

  const allLines = await fetchAllStripeLines(payload, fetchFn);

  // Convert lines to QuickBooks format
  const qbLines = allLines.map((line) => ({
    Description: line.description,
    Amount: line.amount / 100,
    DetailType: 'SalesItemLineDetail',
    SalesItemLineDetail: {
      ItemRef: {
        value: config.serviceItemId ?? '1',
        name: 'Service',
      },
    },
  }));

  // Determine currency from first line (assume all lines same currency)
  const currency = allLines[0].currency.toUpperCase();

  // Build invoice request body
  const invoiceBody = {
    DocNumber: payload.id,
    Line: qbLines,
    Currency: currency,
    CustomerRef: {
      value: config.defaultCustomerId,
    },
    CustomField: [
      {
        DefinitionId: config.customFieldDefinitionId ?? '1',
        StringValue: payload.url,
      },
    ],
  };

  const invoiceUrl = `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/${config.realmId}/invoice`;
  const invoiceResponse = await fetchFn(invoiceUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.accessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(invoiceBody),
  });

  if (!invoiceResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      `QuickBooks create invoice failed: ${invoiceResponse.status} ${invoiceResponse.statusText} at ${invoiceUrl}`
    );
  }

  const invoiceJson = await invoiceResponse.json();
  const invoiceId = invoiceJson?.Invoice?.Id;
  if (!invoiceId) throw new Error('QuickBooks invoice response missing Invoice.Id');

  // Attach Stripe invoice URL as document
  const attachmentBody = {
    AttachableRef: [
      {
        EntityRef: {
          type: 'Invoice',
          value: invoiceId,
        },
      },
    ],
    FileName: 'stripe_invoice.txt',
    ContentType: 'text/plain',
    ByteOrder: 'LittleEndian',
    Content: base64Encode(payload.url),
  };

  const attachmentUrl = `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/${config.realmId}/attachment`;
  const attachmentResponse = await fetchFn(attachmentUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.accessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(attachmentBody),
  });

  if (!attachmentResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      `QuickBooks attach document failed: ${attachmentResponse.status} ${attachmentResponse.statusText} at ${attachmentUrl}`
    );
  }

  const attachmentJson = await attachmentResponse.json();
  const attachmentId = attachmentJson?.Attachment?.Id;
  if (!attachmentId) throw new Error('QuickBooks attachment response missing Attachment.Id');

  return { invoiceId, attachmentId };
}
